### QueueOptions

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.QueueOptions.html

Configuration options for the Queue class.

```APIDOC
## Interface QueueOptions

Options for the Queue class.

```typescript
interface QueueOptions {
  blockingConnection?: boolean;
  connection: ConnectionOptions;
  defaultJobOptions?: DefaultJobOptions;
  prefix?: string;
  settings?: AdvancedRepeatOptions;
  skipMetasUpdate?: boolean;
  skipVersionCheck?: boolean;
  skipWaitingForReady?: boolean;
  streams?: { events: { maxLen: number } };
  telemetry?: Telemetry;
}
```

### Properties

*   **`Optional` blockingConnection**
    *   Type: `boolean`
    *   Description: Denotes commands should retry indefinitely. Deprecated: not in use anymore.

*   **connection**
    *   Type: `ConnectionOptions`
    *   Description: Options for connecting to a Redis instance.

*   **`Optional` defaultJobOptions**
    *   Type: `DefaultJobOptions`
    *   Description: Default options for jobs.

*   **`Optional` prefix**
    *   Type: `string`
    *   Description: Prefix for all queue keys.

*   **`Optional` settings**
    *   Type: `AdvancedRepeatOptions`
    *   Description: Advanced options for the repeatable jobs.

*   **`Optional` skipMetasUpdate**
    *   Type: `boolean`
    *   Description: Skip Meta update. If true, the queue will not update the metadata of the queue. Useful for read-only systems that do should not update the metadata.
    *   Default Value: `false`

*   **`Optional` skipVersionCheck**
    *   Type: `boolean`
    *   Description: Avoid version validation to be greater or equal than v5.0.0.
    *   Default Value: `false`

*   **`Optional` skipWaitingForReady**
    *   Type: `boolean`
    *   Description: Skip waiting for connection ready. In some instances if you want the queue to fail fast if the connection is not ready you can set this to true. This could be useful for testing and when adding jobs via HTTP endpoints for example.

*   **`Optional` streams**
    *   Type: `{ events: { maxLen: number } }`
    *   Description: Options for the streams used internally in BullMQ.
    *   Type Declaration:
        *   `events`: `{ maxLen: number }` - Options for the events stream.
            *   `maxLen`: `number` - Max approximated length for streams. Default is 10 000 events.

*   **`Optional` telemetry**
    *   Type: `Telemetry`
    *   Description: Telemetry client.
```

### DefaultJobOptions Interface

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.DefaultJobOptions.html

The DefaultJobOptions interface defines the configuration options for jobs in BullMQ. These options control aspects like retries, delays, and how jobs are managed upon completion or failure.

```APIDOC
## Interface DefaultJobOptions

### Description
Defines the default options for jobs in BullMQ.

### Properties

- **attempts** (number) - Optional - The total number of attempts to try the job until it completes.
  - Default Value: `1`

- **backoff** (number | BackoffOptions) - Optional - Backoff setting for automatic retries if the job fails.

- **delay** (number) - Optional - An amount of milliseconds to wait until this job can be processed. Note that for accurate delays, worker and producers should have their clocks synchronized.
  - Default Value: `0`

- **keepLogs** (number) - Optional - Maximum amount of log entries that will be preserved.

- **lifo** (boolean) - Optional - If true, adds the job to the right of the queue instead of the left (default false).
  - See: https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/jobs/lifo

- **priority** (number) - Optional - Ranges from 0 (highest priority) to 2 097 152 (lowest priority). Note that using priorities has a slight impact on performance, so do not use it if not required.
  - Default Value: `0`

- **removeOnComplete** (number | boolean | KeepJobs) - Optional - If true, removes the job when it successfully completes. When given a number, it specifies the maximum amount of jobs to keep, or you can provide an object specifying max age and/or count to keep. It overrides whatever setting is used in the worker. Default behavior is to keep the job in the completed set.
  - When using `age` or `count`, the eviction is evaluated on a best-effort basis every time a job finishes; BullMQ does not run a background timer, so aged jobs are only removed once another job completes after their expiration.

- **removeOnFail** (number | boolean | KeepJobs) - Optional - If true, removes the job when it fails after all attempts. When given a number, it specifies the maximum amount of jobs to keep, or you can provide an object specifying max age and/or count to keep. It overrides whatever setting is used in the worker. Default behavior is to keep the job in the failed set.
  - When using `age` or `count`, the eviction is evaluated on a best-effort basis every time a job fails; BullMQ does not run a background timer, so aged jobs are only removed once another job fails after their expiration.

- **sizeLimit** (number) - Optional - Limits the size in bytes of the job's data payload (as a JSON serialized string).

- **stackTraceLimit** (number) - Optional - Limits the amount of stack trace lines that will be recorded in the stacktrace.

- **timestamp** (number) - Optional - Timestamp when the job was created.
  - Default Value: `Date.now()`

```

### WorkerOptions Configuration

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.WorkerOptions.html

This section details the various properties available within the WorkerOptions interface, which are used to configure a BullMQ worker.

```APIDOC
## WorkerOptions

Base Queue options

### Properties

*   **autorun** (`boolean`, optional): Condition to start processor at instance creation. Defaults to `true`.
*   **blockingConnection** (`boolean`, optional): Denotes commands should retry indefinitely. Deprecated: not in use anymore.
*   **concurrency** (`number`, optional): Amount of jobs that a single worker is allowed to work on in parallel. Defaults to `1`. See [https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/workers/concurrency](https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/workers/concurrency).
*   **connection** (`ConnectionOptions`): Options for connecting to a Redis instance.
*   **drainDelay** (`number`, optional): Number of seconds to long poll for jobs when the queue is empty. Defaults to `5`.
*   **limiter** (`RateLimiterOptions`, optional): Enable rate limiter. See [https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/rate-limiting](https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/rate-limiting).
*   **lockDuration** (`number`, optional): Duration of the lock for the job in milliseconds. The lock represents that a worker is processing the job. If the lock is lost, the job will be eventually be picked up by the stalled checker and move back to wait so that another worker can process it again. Defaults to `30000`.
*   **lockRenewTime** (`number`, optional): The time in milliseconds before the lock is automatically renewed. It is not recommended to modify this value, which is by default set to half the lockDuration value, which is optimal for most use cases.
*   **maximumRateLimitDelay** (`number`, optional): Maximum time in milliseconds where the job is idle while being rate limited. While workers are idle because of a rate limiter, they won't fetch new jobs to process and delayed jobs won't be promoted. Defaults to `30000`.
*   **maxStalledCount** (`number`, optional): Amount of times a job can be recovered from a stalled state to the `wait` state. If this is exceeded, the job is moved to `failed`. Defaults to `1`.
*   **maxStartedAttempts** (`number`, optional): Defines the maximum number of times a job is allowed to start processing, regardless of whether it completes or fails. Each time a worker picks up the job and begins processing it, the attemptsStarted counter is incremented. If this counter reaches maxStartedAttempts, the job will be moved to the failed state with an UnrecoverableError. Defaults to `undefined`.
*   **metrics** (`MetricsOptions`, optional): Enable collect metrics. See [https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/metrics](https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/metrics).
*   **name** (`string`, optional): Optional worker name. The name will be stored on every job processed by this worker instance, and can be used to monitor which worker is processing or has processed a given job.
*   **prefix** (`string`, optional): Prefix for all queue keys.
*   **removeOnComplete** (`KeepJobs`, optional): You can provide an object specifying max age and/or count to keep. Default behavior is to keep the job in the completed set. Eviction is evaluated on a best-effort basis when a job finishes, so aged jobs are only removed once another job completes after their expiration.
*   **removeOnFail** (`KeepJobs`, optional): You can provide an object specifying max age and/or count to keep. Default behavior is to keep the job in the failed set. Eviction is evaluated on a best-effort basis when a job fails, so aged jobs are only removed once another job fails after their expiration.
*   **runRetryDelay** (`number`, optional): Delay in milliseconds before retrying a job.
*   **settings** (`AdvancedOptions`, optional): Advanced settings for the worker.
*   **skipLockRenewal** (`boolean`, optional): If true, the lock renewal will be skipped.
*   **skipStalledCheck** (`boolean`, optional): If true, the stalled check will be skipped.
*   **skipVersionCheck** (`boolean`, optional): If true, the version check will be skipped.
*   **skipWaitingForReady** (`boolean`, optional): If true, the worker will not wait for the queue to be ready before starting.
*   **stalledInterval** (`number`, optional): The interval in milliseconds for checking stalled jobs. Defaults to `1000`.
*   **telemetry** (`Telemetry`, optional): Telemetry options for the worker.
*   **useWorkerThreads** (`boolean`, optional): If true, the worker will use worker threads. Defaults to `false`.
*   **workerForkOptions** (`ForkOptions`, optional): Options for forking worker threads.
*   **workerThreadsOptions** (`WorkerOptions`, optional): Options for worker threads.
```
